editorial.blurb: This no-frills Chinatown institution serves impeccable roasted meats and char siu at prices that feel almost impossible—freshly hung barbecue that's tender, well-seasoned, and built to last.
editorial.insiderTip: Arrive early (by 8AM) when the barbecue meats are freshly hung and fully stocked; bring cash only, and order the Combination Rice boxes if you're undecided—three different meats let you try everything at once.

topDishes.note: Classic Peking-style with well-seasoned skin; unbeatable value at $12 for half
Tender, never too fatty—consistently the best in Chinatown
Generous portions with three meats (char siu, crispy roast pork, pig ear) plus house sauce
